children.title: Junior
children.description: Core structures, foundational algorithms, and basic problem-solving patterns.

children.title: Stage 1.1 — Core Data Structures
children.description: Big O, arrays, linked lists, stacks/queues, hash tables.

children.title: Linked Lists
children.description: Singly and doubly linked lists — pointers instead of indices.

children.title: Stage 1.2 — Foundational Algorithms
children.description: Searching, basic sorting, recursion, two-pointer, sliding window.

children.title: Recursion
children.description: Base cases, recursive cases, and tracing a call stack by hand.

children.description: Tracking a moving subrange efficiently instead of recomputing from scratch.

children.title: Intermediate
children.description: Trees, graphs, sorting/searching depth, and an intro to dynamic programming.

children.title: Stage 2.1 — Trees

children.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm

children.description: Merge/quick sort, heaps, binary search on the answer, counting sort.

children.title: Heaps & Priority Queues

children.title: Binary Search on the Answer
children.description: Using binary search on a range of possible answers, not just a sorted array.

children.title: 1D Dynamic Programming
children.description: Fibonacci-style problems, and recognizing overlapping subproblems.

children.title: 2D Dynamic Programming

children.title: Senior
children.description: Advanced DP, advanced graphs, advanced data structures, and algorithmic thinking.

children.title: Stage 3.1 — Advanced Dynamic Programming
children.description: DP on trees, DP on graphs, bitmask DP, optimization techniques.

children.title: DP on Trees
children.description: Carrying state up and down a tree instead of a flat array.

children.title: DP on Graphs

children.title: Bitmask DP
children.description: Using a bitmask as DP state to track subsets efficiently.

children.title: Stage 3.2 — Advanced Graph Algorithms

children.title: Bellman-Ford & Floyd-Warshall
children.description: Shortest paths with negative edges, and all-pairs shortest paths.

children.title: Network Flow
children.description: Max flow / min cut, and the surprising range of problems it quietly solves.

children.title: Strongly Connected Components
children.description: Finding tightly-linked clusters in a directed graph.

children.title: Stage 3.3 — Advanced Data Structures
children.description: Segment trees, Fenwick trees, suffix structures, skip lists.

children.description: Answering range queries and updates in O(log n), built for data that changes.

children.title: Fenwick Trees (BIT)

children.title: Suffix Structures
children.description: Suffix arrays and suffix tries — fast substring search at scale.

children.title: Skip Lists
children.description: A probabilistic alternative to balanced trees, used in real systems like Redis.

children.title: Stage 3.4 — Algorithmic Thinking & Interviews
children.description: System-design tradeoffs, novel problems, mock interviews, clear explanation.

children.description: Choosing a structure based on real constraints, not just "what's fastest."

children.title: Explaining Solutions Clearly
children.description: Communicating a solution's logic and complexity to someone who didn't watch you build it.
